verses.1: And in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message was sent to Jeremiah from God.
verses.2: Take a notebook and write down all the things I have said to you about Israel, about the Jews, and about all the nations since the time when I spoke to you back in the days of Josiah, until today.
verses.3: But may the house of Judah hear all this evil that I am planning to do to them, so that one man after another may turn away from their evil ways. And I will forgive their sins and their transgressions.
verses.4: And Jeremiah called out “Blessed is the son of Nebriah!” Then he wrote down from Jeremiah’s mouth all the words of the LORD that He spoke to him in the book.
verses.5: And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, “I am confined; I cannot enter the house of Jehovah.”
verses.6: And you came and proclaimed in the courts that you had written down from Jehovah’s words, in the ears of the people at the house of Jehovah on that day. And also in the ears of all the Jews who came from their cities.
verses.7: But their camp shall be destroyed before Jehovah, and they shall be forced to turn away from their evil ways. For it is great the anger and the severity of the punishment that Jehovah will bring upon this people.
verses.8: And he did all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him to do, regarding how to read the Book of the Words of Jehovah in the Temple of Jehovah.
verses.9: In the fifth year of Jehoyakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem called for a solemn assembly before the LORD. This happened for all the people who came from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem.
verses.10: And he wrote down the words of Jeremiah in the book. It was written in the court of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, the scribe. The door to the new house of God was opened for all the people to hear.
verses.11: And Micah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the LORD written on the book.
verses.12: And the king’s house descended into the room of the scribe. There, all the officials were sitting: Elishama, the scribe; Delaya, son of Semaiah; Elnanan, son of Akbor; Gamariah, son of Shaphan; and Tzidkiyah, son of Hananiyah. And all the officials were there.
verses.13: And he told them all the things that he had heard from God, through prayer and praise, in the ears of the people.
verses.14: And all the priests sent out to Baruch, son of Nethaniah, son of Semei, son of Kushi. They were told, “Take the gift that you have been asked to bring to the people. Go and take Baruch, son of Neriyah, with you.” So Baruch took the gift in his hands and went to them.
verses.15: And they said to him, “Come and sit with us. Let us call out to you.” And he blessed them with his voice.
verses.16: And when they heard all these words, they were afraid of each other. They said to the prophet, “Blessed be you! Please tell the king all these things.”
verses.17: And he blessed them, saying, “Please tell us how you wrote down all these things.”
verses.18: And he said to them, “Blessed be his name! He will call me all these things. And I will write them down in the book.”
verses.19: And the prophets said, “Blessed be you! You have hidden yourself from everyone. May Jeremiah and no one else know where you are.”
verses.20: And they went to the king’s palace. They placed the documents in Elisa’s office, the scribe’s place. They told the king everything that had been said.
verses.21: The king sent Yehudi to take the gold. Yehudi took it from the treasury of Elišama, the scribe. Then Yehudi called out to the king and to all the officials who stood around the king.
verses.22: And the king shall sit in the throne room in the ninth month. And his brother shall be in a state of panic before him.
verses.23: And it happened that a Jew called out, “Three doors!” And four of them were torn apart by the fire. They were thrown into the fire that burned fiercely. All those who were in the fire were destroyed by the flames.
verses.24: And they did not fear, nor tear off their clothes. The king and all his servants heard all these words.
verses.25: And Elnanatan, Deliyahu, and Gameriyah also fell victim to the king. He failed to burn down the camp, and he didn’t listen to them at all.
verses.26: And the king commanded Ezechias, son of King Hezekiah, and Shearja, son of Azariah, and Selmyah, son of Abedai, to take away the blessed scribe and Jeremiah, the prophet. And Jehovah hid them.
verses.27: And the words of Jehovah were spoken to Jeremiah, after the king had destroyed the scrolls and all those things that Jeremiah had written. These words were given by Jehovah through Jeremiah.
verses.28: Once again, take another piece of parchment and write on it all the same things that were written on the first parchment. This parchment was burned by Jehoykim, the king of Judah.
verses.29: And over Jehoykim, king of Judah, it shall be said: “Thus says the LORD: You have burned down this city. But you know well that it is written about it: ‘When Babylon’s king comes, he will destroy this land, and all its people and animals will be destroyed.’”
verses.30: Therefore, as the LORD said regarding Jehoyakim, king of Judah: He shall not sit on David’s throne. His body will be burned in the day time, and his ashes will be scattered at night.
verses.31: And I appointed him and his descendants, along with his servants, to carry out all the evil that I had spoken about them. They carried out those evil deeds against the people of Jerusalem and against all the Jews.
verses.32: And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch, the son of Neriah, the scribe. And Jeremiah wrote all the words of the scroll on it. These were the words that Jehoiakim, king of Judah, burned with fire. But many more words were added to it later.
